pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# EHL Grand Finale 2026: How to Pick Your Challenge

**Event:** European Hackathon League, Grand Finale (TUM.ai), Garching bei München, 10–11 Oct 2026
**Decision deadline:** **Saturday 13:00.** The team captain selects on ehl.gg, and every team member must be checked in first.
**Scope of this guide:** Atira and Tacto. The BMW challenge has **not** been evaluated yet; see section 8.

---

## 1. TL;DR

| | Atira: "From RFQ to bid" | Tacto: "Negotiation Arena" |
|---|---|---|
| One-liner | Agent clicks through 4 German business websites and submits **one correct, signed bid** | Agent **negotiates by e-mail** with supplier bots and closes the **lowest total-cost deal** |
| Type of problem | Deterministic: exactly one right answer | Strategic: score relative to the best achievable deal |
| Hardest part | Fragile browser engineering | Negotiation judgment on unseen suppliers |
| Harder to implement | **Yes** | No |
| Harder to win at the top | Medium | **Yes** |
| Default pick | Only if the team has a strong browser-automation dev | **✔ Tacto** |

---

## 2. What each challenge actually tackles

### Atira: From RFQ to bid
You are a German hydraulics manufacturer bidding on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. The agent must:

1. Read the tender, the bill of quantities and the bidder Q&A on the **Tender portal** (Vergabeportal). Traps: cookie wall, flaky errors, docs behind an expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, a deadline in another timezone.
2. Find the **current** specification revision on the **Supplier portal**. Traps: it opens the oldest revision first, nested viewers, paged tables.
3. Match materials, stock, lead times and price conditions in the **SAP-style ERP**. Traps: transaction codes, F4 popup, short session timeout.
4. Find the right discount approval and the signing TAN in the **Webmail**. Traps: look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, archive folder, paging.
5. Enter the bid in the configurator and sign it with the TAN.

**The 8 rules** define exactly one correct answer:

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | Quantity = tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification for that position |
| 2 | Requirement comes from the spec revision marked *current* |
| 3 | Material = active ERP material with an exact match on bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification. If one position has none, the answer is `no_bid` |
| 4 | Unit price = condition valid on the tender date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the discount, rounded half-up to the cent |
| 5 | Discount = most recent sales-director approval for *this* tender, otherwise 0 % |
| 6 | Lead time = from-stock if stock covers the quantity, otherwise production lead time |
| 7 | Total = Σ quantity × unit price, rounded half-up |
| 8 | `no_bid` → no positions, total 0 |

**Real-world problem:** autonomous back-office execution across legacy UIs (computer use and RPA reliability).

### Tacto: Negotiation Arena
You are procurement at Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker. Each **case** is one negotiation: a price-increase letter, an expiring framework contract, an RFQ with 2–3 suppliers, or a supplier with a red scorecard. The agent:

1. **Prepares.** It reads the case file and mines the data package: 3 years of POs, invoices, scorecards (OTD, PPM), contracts, market indices, should-cost, call notes and letters.
2. **Negotiates by e-mail.** Each message has a body, up to 3 term sheets, and cited data IDs that the arena checks as verified, contradicted, irrelevant or duplicate.
3. **Closes.** It accepts one supplier term sheet or walks away.

**Score per case** = `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`, clipped to 0…1. C is the total cost: price, uncovered need, payment interest, freight, lead time, quality, index risk and supplier health. A broken must-have scores 0.

**Real-world problem:** autonomous commercial decision-making in procurement. The agent has to read the counterpart, trade the right levers, and know when to walk away.

---

## 3. Formats, scoring and final mechanics

| Item | Atira | Tacto |
|---|---|---|
| Ranking order | Eligible first → quality (0–100) → cost × time | Sum of 5 wave scores (max 500) |
| Practice / feedback | Test runs (max 2 h), 1 submission in flight | 200 practice sessions per 24 h, replay with supplier reasoning, local `arena-sim` |
| Final | 1 run on a **private dataset** after the hackathon (20 min limit) | **Live Final** Sun 12:00, 5 waves × 8 min, no human in the loop |
| Where the agent runs | Their sandbox (tarball + `agent.json`) | **Your machine**, your network, your LLM key |
| Winners decided by | Private run (most weight) + agent architecture + public leaderboard. Exact weights not published | Live Final points → top 10 pitch to the jury (5 + 2 min). Weighting still "placeholder" in the brief |
| LLMs | Free hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next + Cloudflare Clef. Your own key optional. **Cost counts in ranking** | Bring your own key (you pay). **Cost not scored**, but 60 s per message |
| Generalisation risk | Same sites, different data | Up to ⅓ of hidden cases are unseen supplier and case combinations |
| Prize | €1,500 + best 2 EHL finalists → Grand Final | €1,500 + best 2 EHL finalists → Grand Final |

---

## 4. Skills required

Legend: ●●● critical, ●● important, ● nice to have, – not needed

| Skill | Atira | Tacto |
|---|---|---|
| Python | ●●● | ●●● |
| Browser automation (Playwright/CDP, selectors, waits, iframes, popups) | ●●● | – |
| Robust error handling (retries, session timeouts, flaky pages) | ●●● | ●● |
| Document parsing (PDF, ZIP, XLSX, nested viewers) | ●● | ●● |
| Async / parallelism | ●● | ●●● |
| SQL / pandas data mining | ● | ●●● |
| LLM prompt + tool orchestration | ●● | ●●● |
| Deterministic rule / cost engine | ●●● | ●● |
| Procurement / commercial knowledge (Incoterms, payment terms, TCO, tactics) | ●● | ●●● |
| Quality domain (PPM, 8D, scorecards) | ● | ●● |
| SAP familiarity | ●● | ● |
| German reading | ●● | ● |
| Packaging / DevOps (tarball, sandbox env vars) | ●● | ● |
| Pitch / storytelling | ●● | ●●● |

**Ideal team shape**
- **Atira:** 1–2 browser-automation engineers, 1 rule-engine/data person, 1 person who scouts the sites and writes the pitch.
- **Tacto:** 1 backend/async engineer (runner, API, cost calculator), 1 data person (SQL over the package, ID mapping), 1 procurement/negotiation strategist (prompts, lever playbook), 1 pitch person.

---

## 5. Implementation difficulty

| Criterion | Atira | Tacto |
|---|---|---|
| Time to first end-to-end run | Long (4 sites, logins, configurator, TAN) | Short (starter kit plays a case in ~15 min) |
| Number of components | 4 site drivers + rule engine + packaging | Client + data layer + cost calc + LLM negotiator + runner |
| Brittleness | High: one missed popup means no answer | Low: stable API |
| Debug loop | Slow | Fast |
| 0 → 60 % of the score | Hard (all-or-nothing chain) | Easy |
| 60 → 95 % of the score | Medium (precise per-field feedback) | **Hard** (stochastic opponents, unseen types) |
| Silent-failure traps | Wrong revision, superseded approval, wrong price scale → plausible but wrong bid | Wrong data IDs cost trust; broken must-have = 0 |
| Final-day operational risk | Low (their sandbox) | Medium–high (your laptop and network must run unattended) |
| **Overall implementation difficulty** | **Higher** | Medium |

---

## 6. The decision process: run this before 12:30

### Step 1: Hard knock-out questions
Answer honestly. One "no" can decide the choice.

| Question | If NO → |
|---|---|
| Does anyone on the team have **production-grade Playwright/Selenium/CDP** experience? | Strongly avoid Atira |
| Do you have a **paid frontier LLM key** with enough budget for ~200 practice sessions + the final? | Tacto gets harder (open question: are Qwen-class models fast and good enough within 60 s per message?) |
| Can one laptop and network stay **online and unattended Sun 12:00–13:00**? | Tacto final at risk; use a cloud VM or a backup machine |
| Is anyone comfortable with **SQL/pandas** on a multi-table dataset? | Tacto preparation step weak |

### Step 2: Score each challenge
Rate each criterion 1–5 for **your actual team**, multiply by the weight, then sum.

| Criterion | Weight | Atira (1–5) | Tacto (1–5) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Team skill fit (section 4) | 30 % | | |
| Probability of a working end-to-end agent by Sat 20:00 | 20 % | | |
| Ceiling: ability to beat strong teams at the top | 15 % | | |
| Domain edge (procurement / quality / SAP / German) | 15 % | | |
| Final-day operational risk (5 = low risk) | 10 % | | |
| Pitch story / jury appeal | 10 % | | |
| **Weighted total** | 100 % | | |

> Rule of thumb: if the totals are within **0.3**, pick the challenge with the **faster feedback loop** (Tacto). Iteration speed beats raw ambition in a 24 h build.

### Step 3: Reference scoring for a typical team
This assumes a domain-strong, code-moderate team **without** a dedicated browser-automation specialist.

| Criterion | Weight | Atira | Tacto |
|---|---|---|---|
| Team skill fit | 30 % | 2 | 4 |
| Working agent by Sat 20:00 | 20 % | 2 | 5 |
| Ceiling vs strong teams | 15 % | 3 | 3 |
| Domain edge | 15 % | 3 | 5 |
| Final-day operational risk | 10 % | 4 | 3 |
| Pitch story | 10 % | 3 | 4 |
| **Weighted total** | | **2.6** | **4.1** |
| **Recommendation** | | | **✔ Tacto** |

With a strong browser-automation engineer, Atira's "skill fit" and "working agent" scores rise to 4–5 and the gap closes. Re-score in that case.

### Step 4: Sanity checks before committing
- [ ] Opened both starter kits and confirmed they install on our laptops
- [ ] Attended or skimmed the 12:00–13:00 deep dive of the leading candidate
- [ ] Asked the jury how the final score and the jury score combine (unpublished for both)
- [ ] Confirmed whether we are an **invited League finalist**. This matters only for the Grand Final, not for the €1,500 track prize
- [ ] Captain has the ehl.gg login ready and everyone is checked in

---

## 7. Pros and cons

### Atira
**Pros**
- Clear, objective target: one correct answer and per-field scoring
- Free hosted models, and the run happens in their sandbox (no laptop risk on final day)
- The private data has the same sites and rules, so scripted navigation transfers well
- Strong fit for SAP, German and spec-revision (APQP) backgrounds

**Cons**
- Heavy browser engineering, and every trap (cookie wall, timeouts, iframes, ZIPs) must be handled
- All-or-nothing chain: one broken step means no answer
- Slow iteration (1 submission in flight, long test runs)
- Cost × time is ranked, so you can't just throw a big model at it
- Hardcoded answers are rejected, and a coding agent reviews the package

### Tacto
**Pros**
- Running in 15 minutes, with 200 practice sessions per day and replays that explain the supplier's reasoning
- Rewards domain judgment: procurement levers, PPM, 8D, scorecards, TCO
- Partial scores possible; a naive agent already scores something
- Strong pitch material (replays as storytelling)

**Cons**
- Hard to reach the top: stochastic opponents, and ⅓ of the hidden cases are unseen combinations
- You pay for LLM calls; the 60 s per message limit forces a model speed vs. quality trade-off
- The final runs on **your** infrastructure, unattended, with 10 parallel sessions per wave
- Wrong data IDs cost trust, and a broken must-have scores 0
- The cost engine must be code (`total_cost`), not LLM math

---

## 8. Open items and unknowns

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| BMW challenge | **Not evaluated.** Get the brief and add a third column to sections 3–6 |
| Atira winner weighting (private run vs architecture vs leaderboard) | Not published ("exact weights will follow") |
| Tacto track places 1–3 (Live Final vs jury weighting, jury criteria) | Placeholder in the brief, "decided Sat morning" |
| Tacto: when the arena goes offline Saturday night | Announced on Discord |
| Team composition and skills | **Fill in Step 2 with real names** |

---

## 9. First hour after deciding

**If Tacto**
1. Apply for the key at https://arena.tacto.ai/apply and get it approved at the Tacto desk (the key is shown once).
2. Run `git clone https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit.git`, `cd starter-kit`, `cp .env.example .env`, then `uv sync --all-extras`.
3. Run `uv run arena play case:P01` and read the replay together.
4. Split the work: runner + async, data layer + `facts.json` ID index, `total_cost` per term sheet, LLM negotiator prompts.
5. Put Sunday 08:00 (new data release) and 09:00 (pre-flight) in everyone's calendar.

**If Atira**
1. `curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh`, then `atira login`.
2. `eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"`, then click through all 4 sites by hand and document every trap.
3. Fork the starter kit (https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) and get a first test run end to end, even with a wrong answer.
4. Split the work: one driver per site (4 browsers in parallel), plus a deterministic rule engine for rules 1–8.
5. Never tune to the public data; the private run decides.

---

## 10. Sources
- EHL Finale info: https://tum-ai.notion.site/REDACTED
- Atira challenge: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai and https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq
- Atira docs for agents: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt

# Work streams — who builds what, and where the streams meet

Written Sat 2026-10-10 for the three people on the team and for their coding agents. The streams are named after
their owners: J = Julien, I = Ivan, O = Orhun. The short table is in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), section "Who does what"; this file is the detail. If you are a coding agent, read
"How the agent works today", then the section of your human's stream, then "Where the streams meet".

The work is split by files. Each file has exactly one stream that may edit it. That is what lets three people and
their agents work at the same time without merge conflicts and without undoing each other's decisions.

## How the agent works today

Everything submitted to Atira is the folder `agent/`. One run goes like this:

1. `agent.py` reads the run (`run.py`: the brief with the bid rules, each website's address and login, the answer
   schema, the expiry time) and opens one browser tab per website (`browsers.py`, `browser.py`).
2. A **lead model** (`Orchestrator` in `agent.py`) reads the brief. It cannot browse. It has three tools:
   - `investigate(site, task)` sends a **browsing sub-agent** (`BrowsingAgent` in `browsing.py`) to one website with
     a task in plain language. The sub-agent drives the browser through a text view of the page (`observe.js`,
     `Tab` in `browser.py`), takes notes, and returns one text report. Several sites run in parallel.
   - `calculate(expression)` does exact decimal arithmetic (`calc.py`).
   - `submit_bid(answer, hints)` checks the answer against the schema, then sends a sub-agent to type the bid into
     the tender website's form, fetch the signing code from the mailbox, sign and confirm.
3. The lead model decides what to ask next from the reports, works out the bid, and submits.

The run's time is split in `agent.py`: investigations end at 65 % of the working time, from 70 % the lead must
submit, and the bid must be entered and signed by 95 %. In a scored run the working time is what the platform
gives (20 minutes: 13 / 14 / 19). In a test run or a local run it is 10 minutes (6.5 / 7 / 9.5), so a development
run reports sooner; the agent tells the two apart by how far away the platform's expiry is.

What is weak in this design, and why the streams exist:

- The reports are free text. A value that was read wrongly, or from the wrong record, is not caught anywhere.
- The lead model applies about 28 bid rules by itself, one calculator call at a time. Money is scored to the cent,
  and 75 of 100 points sit in the positions.
- The final run uses different websites. Anything that only works because of how the public websites look fails
  there.

## Stream J — sites and reading (Julien)

**Goal.** A sub-agent that is sent to any of the websites with a task comes back with a report that is complete,
exact (values as shown, with units and dates) and says where each value was read. This must hold on software the
agent has never seen.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/browser.py`, `agent/observe.js`, `agent/browsing.py`,
`agent/browsers.py`, `agent/tests/test_browser*.py`, `docs/log/julien.md`.

**What the other streams rely on (do not change without telling stream O first).**
- `Tab(site_id, page)` and `BrowsingAgent(model, tabs, credentials, task, context, name=..., deadline=...,
  max_steps=..., log=...)`, as `agent.py` calls them today.
- `await BrowsingAgent.run()` returns one string: the report, then the notes taken while browsing.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Run one sub-agent per website on your machine with a survey task and compare its report with what you see in
   the browser yourself. Every difference is a bug in this stream.
2. Documents: PDF and ZIP files, documents inside embedded frames and nested viewers. `pypdf` is a declared
   dependency since Sat 14:30; before that every PDF came back as "could not be read" in the sandbox.
3. Lists: paging, "load more", searches that must be narrowed before they show results.
4. Versions: a site that opens an old revision first; the report must say which revision a value comes from and
   which one the site marks as current.
5. Sessions and errors: a session that expires and returns to the sign-in page, error pages that work on a retry,
   popups and dialogs.
6. Look-alike records: the report must name the exact reference, sender and date of what it read, so a record for
   another tender is recognisable as such.
7. Generalisation check: no selector, text, URL or page order that only exists on the public websites. The sign-in
   helper in `browsing.py` finds fields by their type, which is fine; keep it that way.
8. Only when the reports are reliable: fewer steps and tokens per report.

**Done when** a report contains every value the task asked for, as shown on the site, each with its source (page
or document, date, sender, revision), and says plainly what it could not find.

**Not this stream.** Bid rules, arithmetic, the lead model's prompts, the submission flow. Also the pitch and the
development story belong to Julien, outside the code.

## Stream I — bid engine (Ivan)

**Goal.** One function that turns collected facts into the answer object, correct to the cent, with no model
involved. The same facts always give the same bid.

**Files only this stream edits (all new).** `agent/facts.py`, `agent/engine/`, `agent/tests/test_engine*.py`,
`docs/log/ivan.md`.

**What the other streams rely on.**
- `facts.py`: typed records (dataclasses) for everything the rules need. Every fact carries where it came from:
  website, document or record, date, sender, revision. This file is the contract between the streams; a change is
  announced in the first line of the commit message.
- One entry point, proposed as `engine.build_bid(facts) -> dict`, returning an object that matches the answer
  schema in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md), section "Answer schema".

**Rules for the code.**
- `Decimal` only, never `float`. Components stay unrounded; round half-up once at the end (rule 27).
- No model calls, no network, no browser imports. The engine must run in a unit test in milliseconds.
- Tests use invented numbers only. Nothing read from the websites goes into code or tests.
- Missing facts must not crash: a position whose facts are incomplete is left out, and an optional breakdown field
  that is unknown is omitted (omitted means "unanswered", `0.00` means "a known zero"; they score differently).
- If any position has no matching material, the decision is `no_bid` with no positions and total 0.

**Work, in this order.**
1. Read the bid rules in [challenge-atira.md](challenge-atira.md) and the full text with `atira challenge rfq`.
   Write each rule down as one or more cases with invented numbers; these become the tests.
2. `facts.py`, first version, covering the core rules only.
3. Core engine: final quantity (latest clarification, withdrawn clarifications, set-to-piece conversion); price
   condition valid on the scenario date at the highest quantity scale reached; discount (latest approval for the
   exact reference, conditional on a minimum order value); lead time (stock shared between positions of the same
   material, no partial allocation); total; arithmetic consistency.
4. Authority and time as functions over facts: only the latest record not after the scenario date, for the exact
   tender reference, from an authorised sender.
5. Advanced pricing layers, one at a time, each with its tests: which parts the discount applies to, currency
   conversion, metal-index surcharge with validity windows, packaging by carton, shared setup pool, project bonus
   in bands allocated by largest remainders, stroke derived from usable travel.

This stream needs no website, no browser and no test run, so it can start at once. Tell stream O as soon as
`facts.py` covers the core rules; O can then start filling it from the reports.

**Done when** `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes in `agent/` and every rule has at least one
test.

**Not this stream.** Reading websites, prompts, form filling.

## Stream O — lead, submission, runs (Orhun)

**Goal.** The run as a whole: the lead model asks the right questions, the answers become facts, the engine prices
them, and one signed bid is submitted before the clock ends, every time.

**Files only this stream edits.** `agent/agent.py`, `agent/llm.py`, `agent/models.py`, `agent/run.py`,
`agent/calc.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/pyproject.toml`, `agent/uv.lock`, `agent/tests/test_kit.py`,
`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, `docs/` (except the other two push logs).

**Work, in this order.**
1. Baseline: one sandbox test run of the unchanged agent and its score breakdown. It shows where points are lost
   and sets the priorities of streams J and I.
2. Time budget: done Sat 14:30 (see "How the agent works today"). Open: tune the three shares once a run has
   shown how long entering and signing the bid really takes.
3. Deadline guard: the lead is told to submit at 70 % of the time, but if it never calls `submit_bid` the run
   still ends without a bid and scores 0. Make the submission happen without depending on the lead. After the
   bid is accepted the process must exit within 10 seconds.
4. Reports to facts: have the lead model put what the sub-agents report into the records of `facts.py`, and call
   the engine instead of the calculator, as soon as stream I delivers the first version.
5. Submission: the form, the signing code from the mailbox, signature, receipt check; validation against the
   schema read at run time.
6. `llm.py`: when a provider's environment variable is missing it falls back to the provider's public address.
   Model calls must only go through the platform's proxy, so remove these fallbacks.
7. Dependencies requested by the other streams (`pypdf` for stream J is in).
8. `tests/test_kit.py`: three tests still target the starter kit's `solve()` and fail; rewrite them for the
   current `agent.py`.
9. Test runs for all streams, every `atira submit`, Entire and the repository.

**Not this stream.** How a page is read (`browser.py`, `observe.js`, `browsing.py`) and how a price is calculated
(`engine/`).

## Where the streams meet

```
websites ──J──> report (text) ──O──> facts (facts.py, owned by I) ──I──> answer object ──O──> signed bid
```

- **J to O:** the report string from `BrowsingAgent.run()`.
- **O to I:** the records in `facts.py`. I defines them, O fills them.
- **I to O:** `engine.build_bid(facts)` returns the answer object.
- You need a change in a file of another stream: describe it to your human, who asks the owner. Do not edit it,
  not even for a one-line fix; the owner may be changing the same lines.
- You need a new dependency: ask stream O. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` have one owner so the lock file never
  conflicts.
- Local runs with the scouting logins (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`, with `atira models proxy` running) are free
  and unlimited for everyone. Sandbox test runs are limited to two at a time for the whole team and go through
  stream O; ask for one when you need a score.
- Everyone works on their own branch (`stream-j`, `stream-i`, `stream-o`); `main` changes only through pull
  requests. The rules are in AGENTS.md, section "Branches".
- Every push adds an entry to your own push log (`docs/log/<name>.md`, format in AGENTS.md). Read the others'
  new entries after every pull.

## Order of the whole thing (proposal)

1. Now: baseline score (O); core rules as tests and `facts.py` first version (I); per-site report checks (J).
2. Next: core engine wired into the run (I and O); documents and paging reliable (J); second test run.
3. Then: advanced pricing layers (I); submission and deadline guard hardened (O); generalisation check (J).
4. Sunday morning: no new features. The Atira final uses our latest submission that passed review, so the last
   submission before the end must be the most stable one, not the newest experiment. EHL submission is Sunday 12:00.

Captured 2026-10-10 ~11:00 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/ (home, `/challenges/rfq`, `/start`,
`/docs/fair-play.md`, `/docs/faq.md`, `/docs/demo-day.md`, `/docs/building-an-agent.md`, `/llms.txt`).
Extended 2026-10-10 ~12:45 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt (challenge version `6`), which adds
`/docs/scoring.md`, `/docs/run-contract.md`, `/docs/submitting.md`, the answer JSON schema and parts of `/docs/api.md`,
`/docs/cli.md`, `/docs/mcp.md`.
Status: **our track** (team decision Sat 2026-10-10; confirm the selection on ehl.gg before 13:00).
The site is the source of truth — re-read it before building. Not read yet: `/openapi.json`.

## The task in one paragraph

Build an agent that acts as a sales engineer at a German hydraulics manufacturer bidding on a public tender for
hydraulic cylinders. The facts are spread over four German-language web apps. The agent drives a real browser
through them, applies the bid rules, enters **one priced bid** in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with
a TAN from the webmail. No human in the loop. There is exactly one correct answer per scenario.

## The four websites

| Site | Holds | Built-in traps |
|---|---|---|
| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A that changes quantities, bid configurator | Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes, ZIP files, deadline in another timezone |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | Buyer's technical specification and its revisions | Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables |
| ERP | Materials, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | Sales director's discount approval, signing TAN, rule mails (pricing, packaging, FX, setup pools, bonus) | Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

Scouting logins for the public data are published on `/start` (step 3) and exported by `atira scout --env`.
**Do not copy them, or any value from the sites, into the package** (see Fair play).

## Bid rules (condensed; full text of rules 01–29 is on `/challenges/rfq`)

Core:
- **Quantity:** tender quantity, overridden by the latest Q&A clarification for that position. A Q&A answer can
  withdraw an earlier one by number. Convert `Satz` to pieces using the governing specification.
- **Requirement:** from the specification revision marked current, plus Q&A technical amendments that name that
  revision and requirement (latest wins per attribute; others inherited).
- **Material:** the active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly.
  The spec names a Kataloggruppe per requirement; search the ERP by it (searches must narrow to ≤ 20 results).
  If any position has no matching material → **no bid** (no positions, total 0).
- **Unit price:** price condition valid on the scenario date, highest quantity scale reached, minus approved
  discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
- **Discount:** most recent sales-director approval for this exact tender reference, else 0 %. It can be conditional
  on a minimum undiscounted net order value (inclusive threshold; if it fails use 0 %, no fallback to older approvals).
- **Lead time:** from-stock if stock covers the quantity, otherwise production. Stock is shared: sum quantities of all
  positions using the same material; no partial allocation. A Q&A delivery commitment key can override per position.
- **Total:** sum of quantity × rounded final unit price.

Advanced pricing layers (each earns independent credit):
- Konditionsgruppe clauses decide whether the discount applies to base, base + mass surcharge, or neither.
- Currency conversion via an FX key (Devisenfixing mail); metal-index surcharges with validity windows.
- Packaging: carton count = ceil(pieces / carton size) per position, never discounted, never changes bid quantity.
- Shared setup pool fee allocated by quantity × allocation mass; project bonus in marginal bands allocated by
  largest remainders.
- "Nutzbarer Weg" stroke derivation: add twice the per-end reserve from the Technikfreigabe mail, then match the ERP.
- Authority and time: only the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the exact tender reference, from
  the authorized sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation @ the bidder mailbox domain).
- Final price: use unrounded per-piece components, round half-up once at the end.

Partial submission is supported: positions can be explicitly omitted and lose only their own points. The bid must
still be signed and submitted; saving alone scores nothing.

## Scoring and ranking

Ranking order (public leaderboard and final run alike):

1. Eligible before ineligible. **Eligible = the right tender reference.** A wrong decision (bid / no_bid) costs
   quality points but not eligibility.
2. Higher **quality** (0–100).
3. Lower **cost × time**: cost in USD (floor $0.01) times wall-clock seconds (floor 1 s). Both weigh the same;
   halving either halves the product. Among free runs the faster one wins.
4. Submission ID if everything above is equal.

What is measured:
- **Cost:** every model call through the proxy, priced per model at published prices (hosted models at simulated
  prices). Cached input and thinking tokens count. No budget and no spending limit.
- **Time:** from the start of the `run` command until the answer is accepted. Setup and hosted-model warm-up do not
  count.
- A well-formed answer is **final, even if wrong**. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.

Quality for a **bid** case:

| Part | Points |
|---|---|
| Decision | 5 |
| Tender reference | 5 |
| Discount percent | 5 |
| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Dated metal-index check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Positions, split evenly across positions | 75 minus the two checks above when present |

Within one position: material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus
10 %, final unit price 10 %, lead time 10 %. Every field is independent. So 35 % of each position (material +
quantity) needs no pricing at all, and 45 % sits in the four optional breakdown fields plus the base price.

Quality for a **no_bid** case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, total of 0 15.

Details that cost points silently:
- Money is compared **to the cent**.
- Positions are matched by position number; each extra or duplicate position costs one position's share.
- Optional breakdown fields: blank = unanswered (no points, no penalty); `0.00` = a known zero.
- Omitted positions (form option "Position auslassen / Teilpunkte") lose only their own points. The bid must still
  be signed and submitted.

Feedback we get:
- **Test runs** show points per answer field, never the expected values. **Scored runs** show only quality,
  eligibility, cost and time.
- The correct public answer is never published.

Winners (Atira's wording: "roughly in this order"): private dataset → public leaderboard → elegance of the system.

Final run on the private dataset:
- Same jobs, bid rules and answer format; **different software** (layout, navigation, site names), other data, and
  the information split differently across the sites. Each run's brief states the bid rules.
- Runs each team's **latest submission that passed review**, not the best one. Our best submission only holds the
  public leaderboard place. Consequence: never leave an experimental submission as the latest one.
- One attempt by default; **best of three** if opted in before the final starts (team page or
  `atira final --best-of 3`). The single best complete attempt counts, not an average. Own-key model calls can cost
  up to 3×. The choice is frozen when the final starts.
- Our team sees its final logs with private values masked; screens and recordings stay with the organizers.

## Run contract

### Package (`agent.json` at the tarball root)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `setup` | Optional argv array. Runs with network, **without** run variables or team secrets, up to 5 minutes, untimed. Nothing it starts survives into the run. |
| `run` | Argv array. Timed. The clock starts here. |
| `browsers` | Optional whole number 1–4 (default 1). Anything else rejects the package. |
| `models` | Optional list of hosted model ids the run waits for (`qwen`, `clef`). Absent = wait for all; `[]` = start right after setup. Unknown ids reject the package. It only decides the wait. |

- Gzipped tarball ≤ 20 MB, regular files only, no secrets. Both commands run in the package directory.
- `atira submit <dir>` / `atira test-run <dir>` pack the folder and leave out `.git`, `node_modules` and whatever
  `.gitignore` excludes. `?label=` (CLI default: the git commit) tags the upload.

### Phases of a sandbox run

1. **Setup** (untimed, ≤ 5 min, network, no credentials).
2. **Model warm-up** (untimed, ≤ 10 min after setup) for the hosted models listed in `models`.
3. **Run** (timed): scored run **20 minutes**, test run up to 2 hours (keep it under 20 to be safe).

### Inside the run

1. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` returns `brief` (Markdown, with
   the rules), `access` (per site: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials.username/password`), `submission`, `answer_schema`,
   `started_at`, `expires_at`, `spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url`, `llm_providers`, `llm_base_urls`, `llm_env`.
   **Send our own `User-Agent`**: the edge refuses Python's default urllib agent with 403 ("Error 1010").
2. Work the sites with the per-run logins. They only work while the run is live. Site ids: `tender-portal`,
   `customer-portal`, `erp`, `mail`.
3. Answer through the `submission` target. For RFQ it is `{"kind": "site", "siteId": "tender-portal", ...}`: the bid
   is entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with the TAN from the webmail. The API endpoint
   `POST /v1/runs/current/answer` answers `409` for RFQ.
   - Malformed answer: the site shows the validation issues (in German); nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running.
   - Accepted: final, the run ends, token and logins stop working, the agent has **10 seconds to exit**.
4. Building tip from Atira: submit the best answer about a minute before `expires_at` rather than keep searching.

### Environment of the `run` step

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | Platform API and the run token (keep it secret) |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | Same JSON as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL` / `QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL` / `CLEF_API_KEY` | Hosted models through the proxy, run token as key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | Provider bases through the proxy; other providers under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` |
| Team secrets | e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only in the timed run step, redacted from logs |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT` | Browser 1, all browsers as a JSON array, count. Ports 9222–9225 |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1` for browser 1, `:n` for browser n, 1280×800 |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | The only way out: platform, websites, model proxy. CDP stays local |

Locally (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`) there is no run token and no `CDP_URLS`: the agent starts its own browser,
gets `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (brief, access, submission,
answer schema), and the hosted-model variables point at `atira models proxy`. A bid entered with scouting logins is
acknowledged but never counts.

### Sandbox and limits

- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with
  cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq, `xdotool`, ImageMagick `import`.
- Headful Chromium already open; attach with `chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`. Tabs and contexts are free.
  Starting any other browser (headless included) is stopped within seconds and logged.
- One submission in flight per team (next upload gets `429`). Test runs: two at a time, three more may wait.
  Scored runs start before test runs; teams take turns.
- Hosted model outage: retry. If ≥ 80 % of hosted calls failed over at least half the run and it ended without an
  answer, the run does not count and a scored run restarts once by itself.
- Team: up to 5; each person runs `atira login` on their own machine. Team secrets: at most 20, 16 chars – 4 KB.
- Submitting: review (passed / flagged / rejected) → one scored run → leaderboard. A flagged result stays off the
  public board until an organizer passes it. Cancelling a scored run ends that submission.
- **The captain links the team's GitHub repository** on the Atira team page (read-only GitHub App) so the organizers
  can compare a winning submission with its source.

## Answer schema

The tender portal's configurator collects exactly this object; the run's `answer_schema` carries the same JSON
Schema (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false` at both levels). Always validate against the schema read at
run time, not against this table. Largest answer: 65,536 bytes.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tender_reference` | string ≤ 100 | yes | Decides eligibility |
| `decision` | `"bid"` \| `"no_bid"` | yes | no_bid = no positions, total 0 |
| `currency` | const `"EUR"` | yes | All money is net EUR |
| `discount_percent` | number 0–100 | yes | Order-level approved percentage; 0 if none or the condition fails |
| `positions` | array ≤ 100 | yes | One entry per tender position; empty for no_bid |
| `total_net` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Sum of quantity × rounded final unit price |
| `notes` | string ≤ 4000 | no | |

Each entry of `positions`:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | string ≤ 20 | yes | Position number; the scorer matches on it |
| `material_number` | string ≤ 50 | yes | Active ERP material |
| `quantity` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Final pieces (after Q&A changes and Satz conversion) |
| `unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Final unit price, rounded half-up once at the end (rule 27) |
| `lead_time_weeks` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Stock, production or commitment lead time |
| `base_unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | no | EUR scale price per piece before discount (after FX conversion) |
| `surcharge_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Material surcharge + ordinary and allocated setup per piece, before discount, without packaging and bonus |
| `packaging_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Carton cost per piece, never discounted |
| `rebate_total` | number ≥ 0 | no | Project-bonus credit for the **whole position**, not per piece |

Shape (placeholders only, no real values):

```json
{
  "tender_reference": "<reference read from the tender portal>",
  "decision": "bid",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "discount_percent": 0,
  "positions": [
    {
      "position": "<position number>",
      "material_number": "<ERP material>",
      "quantity": 0,
      "unit_price": 0.0,
      "lead_time_weeks": 0,
      "base_unit_price": 0.0,
      "surcharge_per_unit": 0.0,
      "packaging_per_unit": 0.0,
      "rebate_total": 0.0
    }
  ],
  "total_net": 0.0
}
```

## Models

- Free, uncapped, hosted, but **priced into the run's cost at simulated prices**:
  - **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen`; OpenAI-compatible, model name `qwen`, tool calls, images, 256k context):
    $0.15 input, $0.016 cached input, $0.47 output per M tokens; cache writes free; 32 concurrent calls per team.
  - **Cloudflare Clef** (`clef`; multimodal decision model, `POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide` with a state, up to 4
    screenshots and questions of type `choice`, `noul` (yes-probability) or `score`): $0.24 per M input tokens,
    output not priced; 16 concurrent calls per team.
  - Idle models can take minutes to wake; use long timeouts locally. In sandbox runs warm-up is untimed.
- Any other provider with our own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI,
  Together, Fireworks) only through the metering proxy, key stored as a team secret, never in the package.
  Models need a published price and must pass any organizer allowlist.
- Atira's tips: keep what the model reads small, use prompt caching for system prompt and tool definitions,
  re-read a page after every action that changes it.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer reads every package before its scored run)

Rejected or disqualified:
- Hardcoded values from the sites anywhere in code, config, prompts or notes — references, material numbers,
  prices, totals, discounts, logins, TANs — including as defaults or fallbacks.
- Pre-solved answers; fixed click paths; crawlers that collect the sites for one model call.
- Local models in the sandbox, model calls outside the proxy, any other outbound host.
- Text in the package that tries to steer the reviewer.

Allowed: helpers for browser control, parsing a document the model chose, paging a result set the model asked for,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling. Multiple agents and parallel browsers. Knowledge of *how the sites
work* gained from scouting. Facts the brief gives every team (e.g. the sales director's mailbox).

## Local workflow (from `/start`)

1. Sign in with GitHub on the site, create the team, invite teammates by GitHub username.
2. Install the `atira` CLI (Node 24, one file) and `atira login`. Optional MCP: `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp`,
   `codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp` (start test runs, read logs, see browser screens).
3. Starter kit: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz — minimal Python skeleton (`run.py`, `browsers.py`,
   `models.py`, empty `solve()` in `agent.py`); needs `uv` and Playwright Chromium locally.
4. `atira models proxy` in one terminal; `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` then run the agent in another.
5. `atira test-run .` (sandbox, live browser view, logs, recording, score breakdown) → `atira submit .`.

Demo day: best teams run the agent live against the public scenario; prepare a one-line start command and a
fallback recording.

## Assessment for team "Day by day" (Claude's reading, not from the site)

- Scoring is fully objective and automated, with a live leaderboard. No pitch polish can compensate for a wrong bid.
- The hard part is generalization: the final run is on different software, so anything tuned to the public sites'
  selectors or navigation fails. The agent must read pages and decide, with deterministic code only for the maths.
- Sensible split: an LLM navigator per site (up to four browsers in parallel) that extracts structured facts, and a
  deterministic, well-tested pricing engine implementing rules 01–28. The pricing engine is pure code and
  parallelizable across teammates; it is where most of the 75 position points are won or lost.
- Risk: the rule set is large and German-language domain detail is heavy (Konditionsgruppe, Rüstpools, Devisenfixing).
  Partial credit per field makes an incremental approach viable: correct reference + decision + material + quantity
  first, pricing layers after.
- EHL also requires Entire on the team repo and a six-minute pitch on Sunday; how the Atira leaderboard result feeds
  the EHL jury is not stated on the Atira site ("ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes").

Winners (Atira's wording: "roughly in this order"): private dataset → public leaderboard → elegance of the system.

Final run on the private dataset:
- Same jobs, bid rules and answer format; **different software** (layout, navigation, site names), other data, and
  the information split differently across the sites. Each run's brief states the bid rules.
- Runs each team's **latest submission that passed review**, not the best one. Our best submission only holds the
  public leaderboard place. Consequence: never leave an experimental submission as the latest one.
- One attempt by default; **best of three** if opted in before the final starts (team page or
  `atira final --best-of 3`). The single best complete attempt counts, not an average. Own-key model calls can cost
  up to 3×. The choice is frozen when the final starts.
- Our team sees its final logs with private values masked; screens and recordings stay with the organizers.

## Run contract

### Package (`agent.json` at the tarball root)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `setup` | Optional argv array. Runs with network, **without** run variables or team secrets, up to 5 minutes, untimed. Nothing it starts survives into the run. |
| `run` | Argv array. Timed. The clock starts here. |
| `browsers` | Optional whole number 1–4 (default 1). Anything else rejects the package. |
| `models` | Optional list of hosted model ids the run waits for (`qwen`, `clef`). Absent = wait for all; `[]` = start right after setup. Unknown ids reject the package. It only decides the wait. |

- Gzipped tarball ≤ 20 MB, regular files only, no secrets. Both commands run in the package directory.
- `atira submit <dir>` / `atira test-run <dir>` pack the folder and leave out `.git`, `node_modules` and whatever
  `.gitignore` excludes. `?label=` (CLI default: the git commit) tags the upload.

### Phases of a sandbox run

1. **Setup** (untimed, ≤ 5 min, network, no credentials).
2. **Model warm-up** (untimed, ≤ 10 min after setup) for the hosted models listed in `models`.
3. **Run** (timed): scored run **20 minutes**, test run up to 2 hours (keep it under 20 to be safe).

### Inside the run

1. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` returns `brief` (Markdown, with
   the rules), `access` (per site: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials.username/password`), `submission`, `answer_schema`,
   `started_at`, `expires_at`, `spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url`, `llm_providers`, `llm_base_urls`, `llm_env`.
   **Send our own `User-Agent`**: the edge refuses Python's default urllib agent with 403 ("Error 1010").
2. Work the sites with the per-run logins. They only work while the run is live. Site ids: `tender-portal`,
   `customer-portal`, `erp`, `mail`.
3. Answer through the `submission` target. For RFQ it is `{"kind": "site", "siteId": "tender-portal", ...}`: the bid
   is entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with the TAN from the webmail. The API endpoint
   `POST /v1/runs/current/answer` answers `409` for RFQ.
   - Malformed answer: the site shows the validation issues (in German); nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running.
   - Accepted: final, the run ends, token and logins stop working, the agent has **10 seconds to exit**.
4. Building tip from Atira: submit the best answer about a minute before `expires_at` rather than keep searching.

### Environment of the `run` step

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | Platform API and the run token (keep it secret) |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | Same JSON as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL` / `QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL` / `CLEF_API_KEY` | Hosted models through the proxy, run token as key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | Provider bases through the proxy; other providers under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` |
| Team secrets | e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only in the timed run step, redacted from logs |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT` | Browser 1, all browsers as a JSON array, count. Ports 9222–9225 |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1` for browser 1, `:n` for browser n, 1280×800 |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | The only way out: platform, websites, model proxy. CDP stays local |

Locally (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`) there is no run token and no `CDP_URLS`: the agent starts its own browser,
gets `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (brief, access, submission,
answer schema), and the hosted-model variables point at `atira models proxy`. A bid entered with scouting logins is
acknowledged but never counts.

### Sandbox and limits

- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with
  cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq, `xdotool`, ImageMagick `import`.
- Headful Chromium already open; attach with `chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`. Tabs and contexts are free.
  Starting any other browser (headless included) is stopped within seconds and logged.
- One submission in flight per team (next upload gets `429`). Test runs: two at a time, three more may wait.
  Scored runs start before test runs; teams take turns.
- Hosted model outage: retry. If ≥ 80 % of hosted calls failed over at least half the run and it ended without an
  answer, the run does not count and a scored run restarts once by itself.
- Team: up to 5; each person runs `atira login` on their own machine. Team secrets: at most 20, 16 chars – 4 KB.
- Submitting: review (passed / flagged / rejected) → one scored run → leaderboard. A flagged result stays off the
  public board until an organizer passes it. Cancelling a scored run ends that submission.
- **The captain links the team's GitHub repository** on the Atira team page (read-only GitHub App) so the organizers
  can compare a winning submission with its source.

## Answer schema

The tender portal's configurator collects exactly this object; the run's `answer_schema` carries the same JSON
Schema (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false` at both levels). Always validate against the schema read at
run time, not against this table. Largest answer: 65,536 bytes.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tender_reference` | string ≤ 100 | yes | Decides eligibility |
| `decision` | `"bid"` \| `"no_bid"` | yes | no_bid = no positions, total 0 |
| `currency` | const `"EUR"` | yes | All money is net EUR |
| `discount_percent` | number 0–100 | yes | Order-level approved percentage; 0 if none or the condition fails |
| `positions` | array ≤ 100 | yes | One entry per tender position; empty for no_bid |
| `total_net` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Sum of quantity × rounded final unit price |
| `notes` | string ≤ 4000 | no | |

Each entry of `positions`:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | string ≤ 20 | yes | Position number; the scorer matches on it |
| `material_number` | string ≤ 50 | yes | Active ERP material |
| `quantity` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Final pieces (after Q&A changes and Satz conversion) |
| `unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Final unit price, rounded half-up once at the end (rule 27) |
| `lead_time_weeks` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Stock, production or commitment lead time |
| `base_unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | no | EUR scale price per piece before discount (after FX conversion) |
| `surcharge_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Material surcharge + ordinary and allocated setup per piece, before discount, without packaging and bonus |
| `packaging_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Carton cost per piece, never discounted |
| `rebate_total` | number ≥ 0 | no | Project-bonus credit for the **whole position**, not per piece |

Shape (placeholders only, no real values):

```json
{
  "tender_reference": "<reference read from the tender portal>",
  "decision": "bid",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "discount_percent": 0,
  "positions": [
    {
      "position": "<position number>",
      "material_number": "<ERP material>",
      "quantity": 0,
      "unit_price": 0.0,
      "lead_time_weeks": 0,
      "base_unit_price": 0.0,
      "surcharge_per_unit": 0.0,
      "packaging_per_unit": 0.0,
      "rebate_total": 0.0
    }
  ],
  "total_net": 0.0
}
```

## Models

- Free, uncapped, hosted, but **priced into the run's cost at simulated prices**:
  - **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen`; OpenAI-compatible, model name `qwen`, tool calls, images, 256k context):
    $0.15 input, $0.016 cached input, $0.47 output per M tokens; cache writes free; 32 concurrent calls per team.
  - **Cloudflare Clef** (`clef`; multimodal decision model, `POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide` with a state, up to 4
    screenshots and questions of type `choice`, `noul` (yes-probability) or `score`): $0.24 per M input tokens,
    output not priced; 16 concurrent calls per team.
  - Idle models can take minutes to wake; use long timeouts locally. In sandbox runs warm-up is untimed.
- Any other provider with our own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI,
  Together, Fireworks) only through the metering proxy, key stored as a team secret, never in the package.
  Models need a published price and must pass any organizer allowlist.
- Atira's tips: keep what the model reads small, use prompt caching for system prompt and tool definitions,
  re-read a page after every action that changes it.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer reads every package before its scored run)

Rejected or disqualified:
- Hardcoded values from the sites anywhere in code, config, prompts or notes — references, material numbers,
  prices, totals, discounts, logins, TANs — including as defaults or fallbacks.
- Pre-solved answers; fixed click paths; crawlers that collect the sites for one model call.
- Local models in the sandbox, model calls outside the proxy, any other outbound host.
- Text in the package that tries to steer the reviewer.

Allowed: helpers for browser control, parsing a document the model chose, paging a result set the model asked for,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling. Multiple agents and parallel browsers. Knowledge of *how the sites
work* gained from scouting. Facts the brief gives every team (e.g. the sales director's mailbox).

## Local workflow (from `/start`)

1. Sign in with GitHub on the site, create the team, invite teammates by GitHub username.
2. Install the `atira` CLI (Node 24, one file) and `atira login`. Optional MCP: `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp`,
   `codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp` (start test runs, read logs, see browser screens).
3. Starter kit: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz — minimal Python skeleton (`run.py`, `browsers.py`,
   `models.py`, empty `solve()` in `agent.py`); needs `uv` and Playwright Chromium locally.
4. `atira models proxy` in one terminal; `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` then run the agent in another.
5. `atira test-run .` (sandbox, live browser view, logs, recording, score breakdown) → `atira submit .`.

Demo day: best teams run the agent live against the public scenario; prepare a one-line start command and a
fallback recording.

## Assessment for team "Day by day" (Claude's reading, not from the site)

- Scoring is fully objective and automated, with a live leaderboard. No pitch polish can compensate for a wrong bid.
- The hard part is generalization: the final run is on different software, so anything tuned to the public sites'
  selectors or navigation fails. The agent must read pages and decide, with deterministic code only for the maths.
- Sensible split: an LLM navigator per site (up to four browsers in parallel) that extracts structured facts, and a
  deterministic, well-tested pricing engine implementing rules 01–28. The pricing engine is pure code and
  parallelizable across teammates; it is where most of the 75 position points are won or lost.
- Risk: the rule set is large and German-language domain detail is heavy (Konditionsgruppe, Rüstpools, Devisenfixing).
  Partial credit per field makes an incremental approach viable: correct reference + decision + material + quantity
  first, pricing layers after.
- EHL also requires Entire on the team repo and a six-minute pitch on Sunday; how the Atira leaderboard result feeds
  the EHL jury is not stated on the Atira site ("ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes").
